description: [roadmap S3.8] Windows' generic GL leaves out some pixels at the edge of a wide antialiased line's footprint that the port's coverage ramp gives a small coverage (all under 0.13 in the probes): 10 of 12,080 covered pixels in the random-short-line probe (log/roadmap/S3/8_probe.py, scene excl), 40 beyond-one-level pixels of 27,689 in the white-on-black width probe (port/test/test_terrain_overlay.py PINNED widths), always at angles near 45 degrees. The per-column spans measured (log/roadmap/S3/8_probe.py, a8-style listing in 8_notes.md section 2) cut at |offset| 2.0 (width 2, 44-45 degrees), 2.5 (width 3, 40), 3.85 (width 5, 40), 4.0 (width 5, 42-44), 7.0 (width 10, 40), 7.5 (width 10, 44) while the ramp reaches 2.07 .. 7.60; the rule that sets the span (a pixel count per column from the line's fixed-point setup) is not determined. Effect on in-game frames: the census line pixels (8_linegate.tsv) meet G2.
needed: The generic implementation's AA-line span rule (more probes per slope and width, or its code).

description: [roadmap S3.8] The antialiased line model (coverage = clamp(w / 2 + 0.5 - |n|) * clamp(t + 0.5) * clamp(L - t + 0.5) at pixel centres, ends clipped to the viewport then snapped with U-1076's fixed-point setup, width clamped to 10, alpha * coverage blended and dithered as the triangles) is fitted to probes of the real software GL, not read from its code. Residual one-level pixels: 98 of 74,466 changed pixels in the random probe (rand), 48 of 27,689 (widths), 16 of 18,261 (flip); the fully covered interior is exact for every colour and alpha the game passes (36 of 36 colour x alpha blocks, 0 pixels differ).
needed: The generic implementation's coverage arithmetic (fixed-point bits of the distance and of alpha * coverage).

description: [roadmap S3.8] Only the flip-byte-set projection glOrtho(0, 800, 0, 600) occurs in the game: all 25,413 two-dimensional glOrtho calls of the recorded streams (port/corpus/gl/*/stream.gl.txt) have bottom 0 and top 600. The other branch (flip byte clear, glOrtho(0, W, H, 0)) is judged only by the probe scene flip (18 of 18,261 pixels differ, control 4 RED).
needed: None for the game; a recording with the flip byte clear if the port ever runs another window size.

description: [roadmap S3.8] The recorded GL streams keep every call Terrain.dll makes except the vertex data of glBegin..glEnd blocks (gl_rec.js multi mode), so the stream check (log/roadmap/S3/8_streams.tsv) compares each drawLine's count, width, colour and alpha but not its ends. The ends are judged by the frame census only where the line is still visible at a checkpoint (a sprite, a panel or text later drawn over a line hides it).
needed: A recording with glVertex2i kept for drawLine (gl_rec.js keeping the GL_LINES block bodies; NEED_GAME).
